summary: On the pinned 3x600 / 1800-px fixup rig both sides now render a live, 2 Hz beat-locked centred VU meter with falling peak markers in a red-to-magenta palette, but the port draws a fundamentally different picture: the original is INDEX-ONLY (byte-identical flat output on strip, 3x600 and 6x300) with a hard-coded absolute 300-px meter centre, while the port is normalized-coordinate/resolution-independent, and two of the three sliders (SilenceLevel, PeakDropSpeed) are near-inert on the original but dominant on the port.
observations: Both sides are alive and error-free on the fixup rig (grid 3x600, 1800 px, provenance.fixups.rig = {grid, [3,600]}): compileError/runtimeError null, wantsSensors true, sensors 'synth' (beat120) on both. rj-baseline (6 s / 20 fps) orig meanBrightness avg 46.5 max 131, port avg 28.0 max 95. The prior 'original renders nothing' verdict is fully superseded — the original is lively on this rig.

DECISIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING — the ORIGINAL is index-only, the PORT is coordinate-driven. Rendering the same 1800 px three ways (--rig strip --pixels 1800, the pinned --grid 3x600, and --grid 6x300) and diffing the FLAT pixel sequences at t=2.35/3.60/5.85 s: the original's flat sequence is BYTE-IDENTICAL across all three (mean abs diff 0.000 at every time), while the port's changes completely (mean abs diff 21.5 / 65.8 / 18.0 vs strip and 12.4 / 41.4 / 12.4 vs 6x300). The port drives pixels off (x,y); the original drives them off the flat pixel index.

ORIGINAL geometry law (read from --dump on strip at N=900 / 1800 / 3000): it splits the strip into 3 equal segments of pixelCount/3 and draws each meter centred at a HARD-CODED absolute offset of ~300 px from the segment start. At 1800 px that lands exactly mid-segment (flat centres 299.5 / 899.5 / 1499.5). At 3000 px the bars sit at flat centres 299 / 1299 / 2299 (i.e. still +300 into each 1000-px segment, no longer centred); at 900 px each meter's right half is clipped away and the bars end exactly at 299 / 599 / 899. This is the author's 3x600 install baked into the code, and it is exactly why the manifest's 256-px rig produced nothing.

PORT geometry law: fully resolution-independent / normalized. At --pixels 900 and --pixels 3000 on the strip its lit segments occupy IDENTICAL normalized positions (first four segment starts 17/64/123/208 of 900 = 0.019/0.071/0.137/0.231; 57/213/409/691 of 3000 = 0.019/0.071/0.136/0.230). The original has no such invariance.

What each side actually draws on the JUDGED 3x600 rig, steady state (--skip 120, t=120.35 s). ORIGINAL: three horizontal meters stacked down the 600-row axis, identical in all three columns, centred at rows ~100 / ~300 / ~500 — bars at rows 72-126, 272-326, 482-516 plus 1-PIXEL peak-marker dots (rows 13, 213, 386, 466, 532). PORT: one VERTICAL meter per column, all centred at row ~300 — col0 bar rows 254-345 with two 42-ROW-THICK peak-marker blocks at rows 68-109 and 490-531. Same motif, orthogonal layout, and peak markers 42x too thick.

Matched-dial comparison (rj-matched, both sides SilenceLevel=0.5, Fill=1, PeakDropSpeed=0.2, --skip 120): per-channel mean abs diff is 67.3 / 47.5 / 36.1 / 30.1 at t=120.05/0.25/0.35/0.45 s (out of 255), orig window meanBrightness avg 54.2 vs port 27.8. At that setting the port's central bar is gated away completely (only the two marker blocks remain, and column 2 goes entirely black) while the original still draws all three bars.

TIMING — both sides are correctly locked to the 2 Hz beat120 feed. Autocorrelation of meanBrightness over rj-steady (--skip 120, 12 s @ 20 fps) gives a top lag of 10 frames = 0.500 s on BOTH sides (orig r=0.96, port r=0.93), with harmonics at 20/30/40. Attack is one frame, decay spans the 0.5 s interval on both.

TIMING DIVERGENCE — the original's steady state is EXACTLY beat-periodic and melody-blind; the port's is not. Orig meanBrightness repeats the identical 10-frame sequence 18,99,95,92,65,42,31,25,22,20 beat after beat (dumps at 120.05, 121.05, 122.05, 124.05, 128.05 s are byte-identical). The port's beat peaks modulate over the feed's 4 s melody cycle: 101,87,101,87,102,95,... (±8%). So the original's meter levels do not track the stepping melody bin and the port's do.

DECAY RATE — the port's bar and peak markers fall faster than the original's. Steady-state half-widths measured from --dump within one beat (t=+0.25/+0.35/+0.45 s after the attack): orig bar 150 / 82 / 60 px, orig peak-marker radius 291 / 260 / 224 px; port col0 bar 138 / 46 / 15 rows, port marker radius 268 / 211 / 150 rows. The port's bar has collapsed to a quarter of the original's width by +0.45 s.

WARM-UP TRANSIENTS DIFFER. Original (rj-survey300, 300 s @ 10 fps, per-second meanBrightness maxima): rails at 131 for t=0-4 s, then drops to a near-dark 15-16 for t=4-9 s, then ramps 24->109 over t=9-16 s and settles flat at max 99 / avg 57 by ~t=40 s, unchanged out to 300 s. Port: no railed opening and no dark gap — starts at max 46 and rises monotonically, 71 (10 s) -> 98 -> 101 -> 106 -> 109 -> 113 -> 116 -> 119, settling at max 118 / avg 47 only by ~t=80 s. The default 6 s baseline window sits entirely inside both transients, so all headline comparisons above were taken at --skip 120.

PALETTE — same family (red -> magenta), different value/saturation law. The original desaturates toward white as level rises: bar colour runs (255,193,193) when railed, then (255,40,40), (255,19,19), (255,13,13) through the decay; 1-px peak markers are (255,148,148)/(255,100,100)/(255,74,74). The port stays fully saturated: its railed bar is (255,0,0) and its decay colours are (255,11,11)/(255,0,0). Over 60 s the original's meanG avg is 15.9 (max 50) against the port's 4.3 (max 25).

PALETTE — hue spread across the three meters is much wider on the port. Original: meter 1 pure red (255,19,19), meter 2 red with a slight blue tint (255,19,47), meter 3 magenta (255,11,113). Port: col0 red (255,0,0), col1 strong magenta (255,0,107), col2 adds a blue-violet (127,0,255) — an R-halved violet the original never produces at any time or dial setting.

AMPLITUDE PER METER — both sides make the third meter the quiet one (orig block2 bar half-width 9-125 px against blocks 0/1 at 9-300; port col2 similarly the smallest), so the low/mid/high band split reads the same way in character even though the levels differ.

FRAME-RATE COUPLING — both sides are frame-coupled, in OPPOSITE directions. Peak-marker radius at the same absolute time (t~120.35 s) across --fps 10/20/40: orig 282 / 260 / 210 px (markers fall FASTER per second as fps rises), port 163 / 211 / 241 rows (markers fall SLOWER per second as fps rises). Settled window means move the same way: orig 57/51/49, port 47/52/54.
SEED — both sides are seed-independent: --seed 1234 at --skip 120 reproduces seed 1 exactly on both (orig mean 51 motion 17, port mean 52 motion 27, identical to rj-steady).
SENSORS-OFF — matching behaviour: with --sensors off at --skip 120 / 20 fps BOTH sides go completely black (mean 0, motion 0). Neither has a free-running fallback; this axis is correct.

CONTROL SURFACES MATCH EXACTLY: both sides expose sliderSilenceLevel (label 'SilenceLevel'), sliderFill ('Fill'), sliderPeakDropSpeed ('PeakDropSpeed'), all kind 'slider', in the same order. No missing, extra, renamed or retyped control.

UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS DIFFER. Original: setting sliderSilenceLevel=0.5 reproduces the untouched render BYTE-IDENTICALLY (mean abs diff 0.000 at t=120.25 s), pinning its untouched default at exactly 0.5; its untouched PeakDropSpeed sits near 0.2 (untouched markers at rows 8/590 vs 2/596 at v=0 and 17/581 at v=0.5) and its untouched Fill near 1 (closest sweep value, diff 6.5). Port: its untouched SilenceLevel lies between 0 and 0.25 (untouched still draws a central bar 162-437 that is already fully gated off at v=0.25), untouched PeakDropSpeed ~0.07, untouched Fill ~0.9 (between the 0.75 and 1 renders).

Harness/imaging note for a future judge: on a 3x600 grid the contact sheet and filmstrip come out 28x1202 px and the rhythm image collapses to three columns, so all structural claims above were taken from --dump numbers rather than the PNGs. The rhythm images are still useful at a glance and show the headline difference immediately — the original's three columns are indistinguishable (index-only, x-independent) while the port's are red / magenta / near-black.

dials.name: sliderSilenceLevel
dials.origEffect: Essentially INERT on this feed, verified over a 12 s steady-state window (--skip 120) at 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1: window meanBrightness is 51 at every value, and the bar only twitches from rows 149-449 (v=0) to 150-448 (v=1). Probe maxDelta 0.53 (skip 0) / 0.59 (skip 120), below threshold. The untouched default is exactly 0.5.
dials.portEffect: DOMINANT — the strongest dial on the port and monotonic: 12 s window meanBrightness 80 / 38 / 28 / 23 / 20 at 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1. At v=0 the whole meter fills (col0 bar rows 71-528, colour (255,86,86)); by v=0.25 the central bar is gated away entirely and only the two peak-marker blocks survive; at v=1 only markers at rows 122-163 / 436-477 remain. Probe maxDelta 44.10, maxDeltaLit 82.72.

dials.name: sliderFill
dials.origEffect: LIVE and strong — scales the bar's half-width (a gain on the meter). Steady-state bar at t=120.25 s: rows 283-315 (half-width 16) at v=0, 216-382 (83) at v=0.5, 132-466 (167) at v=1; the peak markers ride outward with it (207/391 -> 5/593). 12 s window meanBrightness 8 / 20 / 35 / 46 / 54 across 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1. Probe maxDelta 43.59.
dials.portEffect: LIVE, same direction, slightly compressed range. Col0 bar at t=120.25 s: rows 271-328 (half-width 28) at v=0, 199-400 (100) at v=0.5, 160-439 (139) at v=1. 12 s window meanBrightness 26 / 38 / 47 / 51 / 52 across 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 — the port never gets as dark at v=0 (26 vs the original's 8) and saturates earlier at the top. Probe maxDelta 38.58. This is the one dial that broadly agrees.

dials.name: sliderPeakDropSpeed
dials.origEffect: LIVE but very small — a markers-only effect the probe misses (maxDelta 0.62, maxDeltaLit 1.40, below threshold, because it moves 2 pixels out of 1800). Higher value = peaks fall further/faster: the 1-px markers sit at rows 2/596 (radius 297) at v=0, 17/581 (282) at v=0.5, 31/567 (268) at v=1, while the central bar is unchanged at rows 149-449 for every value. Window meanBrightness is 51 at all five values.
dials.portEffect: LIVE and far too strong — it restructures the whole render, not just the markers. Col0 at t=120.25 s: marker blocks at rows 0-27 / 572-599 (v=0), 30-71 / 528-569 (0.25), 69-110 / 489-530 (0.5), 102-143 / 456-497 (0.75), and at v=1 the markers merge into the bar as a single blob rows 130-469. Probe maxDelta 15.28. Window meanBrightness 51 / 52 / 51 / 48 / 46. Direction (higher = markers closer in) is right; the magnitude is roughly an order of magnitude too large.

feedback: PRIMARY FIX — pixel mapping. The original is index-only: its flat output is byte-identical on --rig strip 1800, --grid 3x600 and --grid 6x300, and it derives everything from the raw pixel index. The port is coordinate-driven and its output changes completely with grid shape. Drive the port off the flat pixel index (not x/y, not normalized 0..1 coordinates) and this whole class of difference collapses.

SECOND FIX — reproduce the original's absolute, hard-coded geometry rather than a resolution-independent one. Measured law: split the strip into 3 equal segments of pixelCount/3, and place each meter's centre at a FIXED offset of ~300 pixels from its segment start, with the bar half-width and the peak-marker radius measured in ABSOLUTE PIXELS (not fractions of the segment). Verify at three sizes: at 1800 px the meters land at flat indices 299.5 / 899.5 / 1499.5 (perfectly centred); at 3000 px they must land at 299 / 1299 / 2299, i.e. NOT mid-segment; at 900 px each meter's right half must fall off the end of its segment so the bars end exactly at 299 / 599 / 899. The port currently keeps identical normalized positions at 900 and 3000 px, which is the opposite behaviour.

PEAK MARKERS are 42x too thick. The original's marker is exactly 1 PIXEL on each side of the bar; the port draws a 42-pixel-wide solid block. Make the marker a single pixel and it also stops merging into the bar at high PeakDropSpeed.

PALETTE — restore the level->desaturation ramp. The original's bar and markers whiten as the level rises: bar (255,13,13) at low level through (255,40,40) mid to (255,193,193) when railed; markers (255,74,74) -> (255,148,148). The port holds pure (255,0,0) at every level (60 s meanG 4.3 vs the original's 15.9). Also narrow the per-meter hue spread: the original's three meters are (255,19,19) / (255,19,47) / (255,11,113) — red, red with a faint blue tint, magenta — while the port spreads them to red / (255,0,107) magenta / (127,0,255) blue-violet. The port should never emit a colour with R below 255 in this pattern; its (127,0,255) violet has no counterpart in any original frame at any dial value.

SLIDER SilenceLevel is wildly over-powered. On the original it does essentially NOTHING with this audio feed — window meanBrightness is 51 at 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1, and the bar moves by one pixel across the whole range. On the port it is the dominant control (mean 80 -> 20, and by v=0.25 the central bar is gated off entirely). Whatever the port is gating on, it is scaling the gate against a far smaller signal than the original does. Also set the port's untouched default to 0.5, which is where the original's untouched render sits exactly (byte-identical at sliderSilenceLevel=0.5); the port's untouched value is currently below 0.25.

SLIDER PeakDropSpeed is roughly an order of magnitude too strong. On the original, sweeping 0->1 moves the peak marker's radius only from 297 px to 268 px (~10%) and never touches the bar. On the port the same sweep moves the marker from radius 286 to fully merged with the bar. Scale the port's drop rate down so the full dial range spans about a 10% change in marker radius, and keep the bar independent of this dial.

SLIDER Fill is close — keep it. Direction and rough magnitude match (orig bar half-width 16/83/167 px at 0/0.5/1; port 28/100/139). Two nitpicks: the port is not dark enough at Fill=0 (window mean 26 vs the original's 8) and saturates early at the top (port 51->52 between 0.75 and 1 while the original still climbs 46->54).

BEAT RESPONSE is right in period but the decay is too fast. Both sides lock to the 2 Hz feed (autocorrelation top lag 10 frames at 20 fps on both). Within one beat the original's bar half-width goes 150 -> 82 -> 60 px at +0.25/+0.35/+0.45 s; the port's goes 138 -> 46 -> 15. Slow the port's bar decay by roughly 2-4x in the second half of the beat interval, and slow its marker fall to match (orig 291/260/224 vs port 268/211/150).

The original's steady state is EXACTLY beat-periodic (its 10-frame meanBrightness sequence repeats byte-identically beat after beat, so its meter levels are melody-blind under beat120), while the port's beat peaks modulate ~8% over the feed's 4 s melody cycle. Whatever spectrum reduction the port uses is picking up the stepping melody bin that the original's does not.

WARM-UP: the original rails at full brightness for the first ~4 s, then drops to a near-dark floor for ~5 s, then ramps up and settles by ~t=40 s. The port has no railed opening and no dark gap — it ramps monotonically from t=0 and does not settle until ~t=80 s. Whatever running average / AGC the port uses is initialised differently and has roughly twice the original's time constant. Note this means the default 6 s window is not a valid place to judge this pattern: use --skip 120 or later.

FRAME-RATE COUPLING: both sides are frame-coupled but in opposite directions (peak radius at a fixed absolute time, --fps 10/20/40: orig 282/260/210, port 163/211/241). Once the drop rate is retuned, check the sign — the original decrements the peak per rendered frame in a way that makes it fall faster in wall-clock terms as fps rises; the port currently does the reverse.

Two axes are already correct and should not be regressed: both sides render fully black with --sensors off (no free-running fallback), and both are seed-independent (--seed 1234 reproduces --seed 1 byte-for-byte at --skip 120). The control surface also already matches exactly (three sliders, same names, same kinds, same order).
